name: Foreign Institutional Investors (FII/FPI)
summary: Foreign corporates/funds/individuals investing in India in large size; flows impact sentiment.
bot_use: Track FII net buy/sell flows as a sentiment input.

name: Company Funding Lifecycle
summary: Seed (promoter + angels) -> Series A (VC) -> Series B -> Series C (Private Equity) -> IPO; valuation rises as revenue/profit validate business.

name: Initial Public Offering (IPO)
summary: First offer of a company's shares to the public, moving it from private to listed (primary -> secondary market).
bot_use: Subscription multiple and anchor/VC pedigree are pre-listing sentiment features; listing day = start of secondary trading.
caveats: Investors should read the DRHP; some companies list without healthy prior funding rounds.

name: What Moves Stock Prices
summary: Prices move on news/events (company, industry, economy) and expectations, and on demand-supply imbalance even without news.
bot_use: News/event sentiment and sector contagion features; liquidity filter - illiquid names don't respond.

name: Absolute Return
summary: Percentage gain irrespective of time.

name: Compounded Annual Growth Rate (CAGR)
summary: Annualised growth rate over multiple years.

name: Stock Market Index (Nifty / Sensex)
summary: Basket of large, liquid stocks acting as a barometer of the market/economy; Nifty (NSE) and Sensex (BSE).
bot_use: Benchmark strategy returns against Nifty; use index as regime/market-trend filter; hedge with index futures.

name: Free Float Market Capitalisation
summary: Market value of shares available for trading; basis of Indian index weights.

name: 52-Week High / Low and All-Time High / Low
summary: Highest/lowest traded price over last 52 weeks (or since listing).
bot_use: Breakout/momentum filter.

name: Order Types (Limit, Market, SL, SL-M)
summary: Limit = specific price (may not fill); Market = immediate at available prices (price uncertainty); SL/SL-M = passive stop that activates at trigger price.
bot_use: Prefer limit orders to control slippage; place SL/SL-M orders immediately after entry.

name: Bid, Ask and Market Depth
summary: Bid = best prices buyers will pay; ask/offer = prices sellers demand; depth shows top 5 levels each side.
bot_use: Estimate slippage by walking the depth for order size; use bid/ask totals as order-flow imbalance feature.

name: Transaction Charges (brokerage, STT, exchange fees, GST, SEBI fees, stamp duty)
summary: Costs on every trade - brokerage, Securities Transaction Tax, exchange transaction charges, service tax/GST, SEBI turnover fee.
bot_use: Always deduct full round-trip costs in backtests; costs dominate high-frequency strategies.
caveats: Rates in source are dated; use current schedule.

name: Corporate Actions
summary: Board-initiated, shareholder-approved actions that change the stock - dividends, bonus, split, rights, buyback.
bot_use: Adjust historical prices for splits/bonuses; flag ex-dates to avoid false gaps in signals.

name: Dividend
summary: Distribution of profits (or reserves) per share, expressed as % of face value; interim or final.
bot_use: Price drops roughly by dividend amount on ex-date - adjust backtests; dividend arbitrage awareness.

name: Bonus Issue
summary: Free shares from reserves in a fixed ratio (e.g. 2:1 = 2 new per 1 held); share count rises, price adjusts, value unchanged.

name: Stock Split
summary: Face value split (e.g. FV 10 -> 5); shares multiply, price divides, market cap unchanged.

name: RBI Monetary Policy (Repo, Reverse Repo, CRR)
summary: RBI balances growth vs inflation via key rates; reviewed periodically (quarterly per source).
bot_use: Event-day volatility regime; sector rotation on rate decisions.

name: Purchasing Managers Index (PMI)
summary: Survey-based manufacturing/services activity index.

name: Quarterly Earnings Announcement
summary: Listed companies report quarterly revenue, expenses, taxes, profit and sometimes guidance.
bot_use: Earnings-surprise strategies; avoid holding through results unless intended; widen stops/IV crush awareness.

name: Point of View (POV) and Instrument Selection
summary: Success requires a researched directional view (via FA, TA, quant) plus choosing the right instrument to express it.
bot_use: Map signal horizon/conviction to instrument - equity for long-term, futures for short-term directional, options for capped-risk/event trades.

name: Japanese Candlestick Anatomy
summary: Real body connects open and close; upper shadow to high, lower shadow to low; bullish (blue/green) if close > open, bearish (red) if close < open.

name: Candlestick Trading Rules (3 assumptions)
summary: (1) Buy strength, sell weakness - buy on a blue day, sell on a red day; (2) be flexible but quantify and verify deviations; (3) look for a prior trend - bullish patterns need a prior downtrend, bearish need a prior uptrend.
bot_use: Implement pattern detectors with tolerance params; require prior trend filter; enter at close of signal bar (aggressive) or next bar close with colour confirmation (conservative).

name: Prior Trend Requirement
summary: Reversal patterns are valid only after an opposing trend; a perfect hammer without a prior downtrend is not a pattern.

conditions.prior_downtrend_proxy: close[t-1] < close[t-1-n] (e.g. n=5..10) or close below falling short EMA
conditions.prior_uptrend_proxy: close[t-1] > close[t-1-n] or close above rising short EMA

caveats: Source defines prior trend visually; the proxies are implementation choices.

name: Bullish Marubozu
summary: Long blue candle with no shadows (open = low, close = high) showing buying at every price; bullish regardless of prior trend.

conditions.identify: close > open and abs(open - low) <= tol*high and abs(high - close) <= tol*high
conditions.entry: near close of marubozu (risk taker) or next day close if next day is blue (risk averse)

name: Bearish Marubozu
summary: Long red candle with no shadows (open = high, close = low); extreme selling; bearish regardless of prior trend.

conditions.identify: close < open and abs(high - open) <= tol*high and abs(close - low) <= tol*high
conditions.entry: short near close (or next day close if red)

name: Spinning Top
summary: Small real body with roughly equal upper and lower shadows; colour irrelevant; indecision - bulls and bears both failed.

conditions.identify: body small relative to range and upper_shadow ~= lower_shadow

bot_use: Treat as volatility-expansion/indecision flag; reduce size or scale out; not an entry signal alone.

name: Doji
summary: Open ~= close (no or wafer-thin body), shadows any length; indecision like spinning top; often appear in clusters.

name: Paper Umbrella
summary: Small body near top of range with long lower shadow >= 2x body; called Hammer after a downtrend, Hanging Man after an uptrend.

name: Hammer
summary: Paper umbrella at the bottom of a downtrend; bulls rejected new lows; bullish reversal. Longer lower shadow = more bullish; blue body slightly preferred.

conditions.identify: lower_shadow >= 2*body and abs(close-open)/open within ~1-2% and close near high
conditions.entry: near close of hammer day (risk taker) or next day close if blue (risk averse)

name: Hanging Man
summary: Paper umbrella at the top of an uptrend; bears entered intraday; bearish reversal (less reliable than hammer per author because price recovered).

conditions.entry: short near close (or next day close if red)

name: Shooting Star
summary: Inverted umbrella at top of uptrend - small body near low with upper shadow >= 2x body; bears pushed price back from new high; bearish. Red body slightly more reliable.

conditions.identify: upper_shadow >= 2*body and lower_shadow small and close ~= low
conditions.entry: short near close (or next day if red)

name: Bullish Engulfing
summary: Two-candle bottom reversal - P1 red, P2 blue whose real body engulfs P1's real body.

conditions.identify: P1.close < P1.open and P2.close > P2.open and P2.open <= P1.close and P2.close > P1.open
conditions.entry: close of P2 (preferred - multi-day pattern) or day after if blue

name: Bearish Engulfing
summary: Two-candle top reversal - P1 blue, P2 red whose body engulfs P1's body.

conditions.identify: P1.close > P1.open and P2.close < P2.open and P2.open >= P1.close and P2.close < P1.open

name: Piercing Pattern
summary: Like bullish engulfing but P2's blue body covers 50% to <100% of P1's red body.

conditions.identify: P1 red, P2 blue, 0.5*P1.body <= (P2.close - P1.close) < P1.body

name: Dark Cloud Cover
summary: Like bearish engulfing but P2's red body covers 50% to <100% of P1's blue body; trade setup same as bearish engulfing.

conditions.identify: P1 blue, P2 red, 0.5*P1.body <= (P1.close - P2.close) < P1.body

name: Bullish Harami
summary: Bottom reversal - long red P1 then small blue P2 contained within P1's body ('pregnant'); surprise strength unnerves bears.

conditions.identify: P1 long red; P2 blue; P2.open > P1.close; P2.close < P1.open
conditions.entry: close of P2 or next day if blue

name: Bearish Harami
summary: Top reversal - long blue P1 then small red P2 inside P1's body.

conditions.identify: P1 long blue; P2 red; P2.open < P1.close; P2.close > P1.open
conditions.entry: short at close of P2 or next day if red

name: Gap Up / Gap Down
summary: Gap up = open above prior close (buyer enthusiasm, bullish); gap down = open below prior close (bearish); no trades occur in the gap.

name: Morning Star (and Morning Doji Star)
summary: Three-candle bottom reversal - long red P1, gap-down doji/spinning top P2, gap-up blue P3 closing above P1's open.

conditions.identify: P1 red (long); P2 gaps down and is doji/spinning top; P3 gaps up, blue, P3.close > P1.open
conditions.entry: close of P3 for both risk types

name: Evening Star (and Evening Doji Star)
summary: Three-candle top reversal - long blue P1, gap-up doji/spinning top P2, gap-down red P3 closing below P1's open.

conditions.identify: P1 blue; P2 gaps up, doji/spinning top; P3 gaps down, red, P3.close < P1.open

name: Support and Resistance (S&R)
summary: Price zones expected to attract maximum buying (support, below CMP) or selling (resistance, above CMP); used for targets, entries and stop placement.

conditions.level_valid: count(swing pivots within +/-tol of level) >= 3 and pivots spaced in time

bot_use: Detect swing pivots, cluster by price with tolerance, keep clusters with >=3 well-spaced touches; use nearest opposite level as target and require stop near a level.

name: Volume and the Volume-Price Trend Table
summary: Shares traded (one buy + one sell of 100 = volume 100); used to confirm trends; high volume implies institutional 'smart money'.

conditions.price_up_vol_down: caution - weak hands buying / possible bull trap
conditions.price_down_vol_down: caution - weak hands selling / possible bear trap

bot_use: Volume filter for entries - require volume >= 10-day average on the signal bar.

name: Moving Averages (SMA / EMA)
summary: Rolling average of closes; SMA weights equally, EMA weights recent data more and reacts faster (preferred). Lagging trend-following tool.

name: Price vs 50-day EMA System
summary: Long when close crosses above 50 EMA; exit when close crosses below.
caveats: Many marginal/losing signals in sideways markets.

name: Moving Average Crossover System
summary: Long when fast EMA crosses above slow EMA; exit when fast crosses below; fewer whipsaws than single MA.
bot_use: Baseline trend-following strategy; combine with ADX/regime filter to avoid sideways whipsaw.

name: Relative Strength Index (RSI)
summary: J. Welles Wilder's 0-100 momentum oscillator of internal strength; strongest in sideways markets.

conditions.persistent_overbought: RSI stuck > 70 for long -> look to BUY (excess positive momentum)
conditions.persistent_oversold: RSI stuck < 30 for long -> look to SELL
conditions.exit_oversold: RSI crosses back above 30 after prolonged oversold -> long
conditions.exit_overbought: RSI crosses back below 70 after prolonged overbought -> short

name: MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence)
summary: Gerald Appel's momentum/trend indicator - MACD line = 12 EMA - 26 EMA; signal line = 9-period EMA of MACD.

name: Bollinger Bands
summary: John Bollinger's 20 SMA with +/-2 standard deviation bands; mean-reversion tool.

conditions.short: price touches upper band -> target middle
conditions.long: price touches lower band -> target middle
conditions.failure: envelope expansion (bands widening as price rides a band) = trending market, signals fail

name: Fibonacci Retracements
summary: After a sharp move (trough to peak = 100%), price tends to retrace to 23.6%, 38.2% or 61.8% before resuming the trend.

name: Double / Triple Top and Bottom
summary: Reversal patterns where a price level is tested twice (or thrice) with tests well spaced in time (>= ~2 weeks); triple is stronger than double.

conditions.double_bottom: two lows within tolerance, separated by >= ~10 sessions with a rebound between -> bullish
conditions.double_top: two highs within tolerance (e.g. 336 vs 332 accepted) -> bearish

name: Range Breakout / Breakdown
summary: Breakout of a range often starts a new trend; true breakouts have high volume and high momentum; false breakouts have low volume and fall back into range.

conditions.entry_long: close > range_high with volume > avg volume

name: Flag Formation
summary: Steep rally (pole) then 5-15 session low-volume correction in a parallel channel; price then resumes sharply upward - second chance to buy.

conditions.identify: sharp rally then 5-15 bar pullback within parallel lines on declining volume

name: Reward-to-Risk Ratio (RRR)
summary: Expected reward per unit of risk; trades below your RRR threshold must be dropped regardless of setup quality.

name: Grand 6-Point TA Checklist
summary: (1) recognisable candlestick pattern; (2) stop near S&R (long - pattern low near support; short - pattern high near resistance); (3) volume >= 10-day average; (4) Dow Theory context (primary/secondary trend, double/triple/range/flag); (5) indicators (RSI/MACD) confirm -> scale size up, else proceed at reduced size; (6) RRR >= threshold (1.5 for active traders).

conditions.indicator_rule: if indicators confirm: size = full (e.g. 500); else size = reduced (e.g. 300)
conditions.trade_quality: satisfy at least 3-4 checklist points; prefer stock with more points over prettier pattern

bot_use: Encode as a scoring function; hard filters for 1,2,3,6 and size multiplier for 5.

name: Swing Trade Scanning Process
summary: Universe Nifty 50, EOD charts, 6-12 month look-back (2 yr for S&R); Part 1 shortlist charts with a pattern in last 3-4 candles; Part 2 evaluate 4-5 shortlisted charts against checklist; at most 1-2 qualify.
bot_use: Direct blueprint for an EOD scanner pipeline.

name: Opportunity Universe
summary: Fixed list of liquid stocks you scan daily (e.g. Nifty 50).

conditions.liquidity: avg daily volume >= 500000 or tight bid-ask spread

name: ADX / +DI / -DI (Directional Movement)
summary: Wilder's trend-strength system; ADX measures strength (not direction), +DI/-DI give direction.

conditions.stop: low (long) / high (short) of signal candle; trade valid until stop breached

bot_use: Regime filter - enable trend systems when ADX > 25, mean-reversion when ADX < 20.

name: Alligator (Bill Williams)
summary: Three displaced SMAs - jaw 13, teeth 8, lips 5.

conditions.buy: close > SMA5 > SMA8 > SMA13 and lines separated
conditions.sell: close < SMA5 < SMA8 < SMA13 and lines separated

name: Aroon and Aroon Oscillator
summary: Tushar Chande's time-since-high/low indicator (0-100); default 25 (Kite 14).

name: Average True Range (ATR)
summary: Wilder's volatility measure including gaps; no direction; in price units.

formula.atr: Wilder smoothing / average of TR over n

conditions.skip: if ATR-based stop violates RRR, skip trade

bot_use: Volatility-normalised stops and position sizing.

name: Supertrend
summary: ATR-based trailing trend line (Kite default period 7, multiplier 3); green below price in uptrends, red above in downtrends.

conditions.trail: hold long until close below green line

name: VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price)
summary: Intraday cumulative volume-weighted typical price; gauges intraday direction and execution quality.
caveats: Intraday only; ignore jump at 9:15 open; lags price.

name: Core-Satellite Capital Allocation
summary: Split capital (e.g. 60/40) - core in fundamentally strong long-term holdings (expect 12-15% CAGR), satellite for active TA trading in equity/F&O (expect 10-12% absolute/yr).
bot_use: Allocate a capped satellite bucket to algorithmic strategies while core remains long-term.

name: Compounding Effect
summary: Reinvesting gains lets money grow on itself; the longer you stay invested, the faster absolute wealth grows.

name: Profit & Loss Statement (Income Statement)
summary: Revenue, expenses, tax and EPS for a period (year/quarter); top line = revenue, bottom line = PAT.

formula.net_revenue_from_ops: sale of products (net of excise) + services + other operating revenue

name: Balance Sheet
summary: Cumulative (flow-basis) statement of assets, liabilities and shareholders' equity; Assets = Liabilities + Equity.

name: Cash Flow Statement
summary: True cash generated/consumed across operating, investing and financing activities; net cash flow ties to balance sheet cash.

name: EBITDA and EBITDA Margin
summary: Operating profitability excluding other income, finance cost and D&A; reflects management efficiency.

name: PAT Margin (Net Profit Margin)
summary: Overall profitability after all expenses and tax.

name: Return on Equity (RoE)
summary: Profit per unit of shareholders' equity; key investable attribute. Top Indian companies average 14-16%; author prefers >18-20% (checklist >25%) without high debt.
caveats: Debt inflates RoE (pizza oven example 25% -> 31% -> 50% as debt rises); always inspect with DuPont and debt levels.

name: DuPont Model
summary: RoE = Net profit margin x Asset turnover x Financial leverage; reveals quality of returns.

name: Return on Assets (RoA)
summary: Efficiency of asset use, adding back after-tax interest (tax shield) since lenders fund assets.

name: Return on Capital Employed (ROCE)
summary: Return on total capital (debt + equity).

name: Interest Coverage Ratio
summary: Ability to service interest from operating earnings; low coverage = default risk.

name: Debt to Equity Ratio
summary: Total (short + long-term) debt relative to equity; >1 indicates high leverage.

name: Debt to Asset Ratio
summary: Share of assets financed by debt.

name: Financial Leverage Ratio
summary: Assets supported per unit of equity; higher = more leveraged.

name: Operating (Activity / Management) Ratios
summary: Efficiency of converting assets into revenue.

formula.cogs: materials + stock-in-trade purchases + stores & spares + power & fuel

caveats: High inventory turnover could reflect low production capacity - investigate funding
raw material access
scalability.

name: Asset Turnover
summary: Revenue generated per rupee of average total assets.

name: Gross Profit Margin
summary: (Net sales - COGS)/Net sales; >20% suggests a moat.

name: Earnings Per Share (EPS)
summary: PAT per outstanding share; EPS growth should track PAT growth (else dilution).

name: Price to Sales (P/S)
summary: Price relative to sales per share; useful when earnings are cyclical or distorted.
caveats: Higher-margin firms justify higher P/S - check profit margin.

name: Price to Book Value (P/BV)
summary: Price relative to book (liquidation) value per share.

name: Price to Earnings (P/E)
summary: Price paid per rupee of earnings - the 'financial ratio superstar'.

name: Nifty Index Valuation (P/E bands)
summary: Nifty P/E historically 16-20x (avg ~18x); peaked 28x (Jan 2008, pre-crash), troughed ~11x (late 2008/09).
bot_use: Macro valuation regime filter for long-only equity allocation / leverage.
caveats: Bands are from source era (2014); P/E methodology changed to consolidated earnings in 2021 - recalibrate.

name: 10-Point Fundamental Checklist
summary: Screen for investable-grade financials.

conditions.revenue_and_pat_growth: in line with each other; author prefers revenue & PAT CAGR > 15%
conditions.eps: EPS growth consistent with net profit growth (no dilution)
conditions.debt: not highly leveraged; track Debt/EBIT trend and interest coverage
conditions.inventory: manufacturing - inventory growing with PAT; stable/declining inventory days
conditions.sales_vs_receivables: sales not driven by receivables (receivables % of sales stable/declining)

bot_use: Direct screener rules for a fundamental-filtered universe.

name: Time Value of Money (FV, PV, NPV)
summary: Money's value changes over time due to opportunity cost; compounding moves money forward, discounting moves it back.

name: Free Cash Flow (FCF)
summary: Operating cash after capex - cash available to shareholders; mark of a healthy business.

name: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Valuation
summary: Intrinsic value = PV of projected FCF + PV of terminal value, adjusted for net debt, divided by shares.

formula.base_fcf: average FCF of last 3 years (smooths cyclicality)
formula.projection: stage 1 (yrs 1-5) growth g1 (e.g. 18%, 15% for large caps), stage 2 (yrs 6-10) g2 (e.g. 10%)

conditions.hold: lower band <= price <= upper band (no fresh buy)
conditions.overvalued: price > upper band (book profits or hold, never buy)

caveats: Garbage in, garbage out - requires forecasting.
Highly sensitive to terminal growth (3.5% -> 4% moves value 368 -> 394).
Needs constant updates; useless for <1 yr horizon.
Keep assumptions conservative - FCF growth <= 20%, terminal growth <= 4%, 10-year 2-stage.

name: Margin of Safety
summary: Benjamin Graham's principle - buy only at a discount to intrinsic value; author takes a further >= 30% discount to the lower value band.

name: Futures Contract
summary: Exchange-traded, standardised, SEBI-regulated, transferable, time-bound, mostly cash-settled agreement whose price mimics the underlying.
bot_use: Express short-term directional views with leverage; trade shorts overnight; hedge portfolios.

name: Leverage
summary: Controlling a large contract value with a small margin; double-edged - magnifies gains and losses.
bot_use: Cap effective leverage (e.g. <= 10x); compute margin-wipeout distance before entry.

name: Margins (Initial, SPAN, Exposure, Maintenance)
summary: Initial margin = SPAN + exposure, blocked while position is open; SPAN (exchange minimum, volatility-driven) acts as maintenance margin; exposure ~4-5% of CV extra cushion.
caveats: Margin rules changed after 2020 SEBI peak-margin regime; intraday leverage limits differ now.

name: Mark to Market (M2M)
summary: Daily settlement of futures P&L using previous close as reference; reference price resets to each day's close.

formula.daily_m2m: (close_t - ref_price) * qty * direction, ref = entry on day 1 else close_{t-1}

name: Margin Call
summary: When cash balance after M2M falls below SPAN (maintenance) margin, broker demands funds or force-closes positions.
bot_use: Monitor margin utilisation intraday; reduce positions before forced liquidation.

name: Trailing Stop Loss
summary: Move the stop in the trade's favour as price advances to lock in profit and ride momentum beyond the original target.

conditions.step_rule: for every N points of favourable move, raise stop by N (example N=15)

bot_use: Implement fixed-step, ATR-based or Supertrend trailing stops.

name: Nifty (Index) Futures
summary: Futures on the Nifty index; most liquid derivative in India.
bot_use: Preferred instrument for systematic index strategies and portfolio hedges.

name: Impact Cost
summary: Round-trip loss (buy at best ask, sell at best bid) as % of mid price; proxy for liquidity and market-order slippage.
bot_use: Slippage model in backtests; liquidity filter for universe.

name: Futures Pricing (Spot-Futures Parity)
summary: Futures fair value = spot adjusted for risk-free carry minus dividends; basis (spread) = futures - spot; converges to zero at expiry.

name: Cash & Carry Arbitrage
summary: When futures trade far above fair value, buy spot and sell futures to lock the spread; unwind near expiry as prices converge.

conditions.exit: just before expiry (sell spot, buy futures)

name: Calendar Spread (Futures)
summary: Buy one expiry and sell another of the same underlying when their spread deviates from fair value; sell the expensive, buy the cheap.

conditions.entry: near-month trades far above fair value while mid-month near fair -> short near, long mid
conditions.assumption: mid month stays near fair value; near converges to spot at expiry

name: Hedging
summary: Taking an offsetting position to insulate an existing position from adverse moves (like a fence around a garden).

name: Beta
summary: Sensitivity of a stock's returns to market returns; market beta = 1; <1 low beta, >1 high beta, <0 inverse.

name: Portfolio Hedge with Nifty Futures
summary: Short beta-weighted value of Nifty futures to neutralise systematic risk of a long portfolio.
bot_use: Automated beta-hedging overlay for long equity books.
caveats: Fractional lots impossible - perfect hedge rarely possible.

name: Open Interest (OI)
summary: Number of outstanding (open) derivative contracts; rises when new positions are created, falls when positions are closed, unchanged on transfers. Continuous across days unlike volume.

conditions.short_covering: price up & OI down -> shorts covering (bearish trend may end)
conditions.long_unwinding: price down & OI down -> longs exiting (bullish trend may end)
conditions.caution: abnormally high OI with rapid price move = euphoria/leverage; small trigger can cause panic

bot_use: Classify each bar as long buildup/short buildup/short covering/long unwinding as a positioning feature.

name: Call Option (long and short)
summary: Buyer bullish with limited risk (premium) and unlimited upside; seller expects price not to rise above strike, earns limited premium with unlimited risk and must post futures-like margin.

name: Put Option (long and short)
summary: Buyer bearish - right to sell at strike; seller bullish/neutral, earns limited premium with large risk.

name: Moneyness (ITM / ATM / OTM)
summary: ITM has positive intrinsic value; ATM strike is nearest to spot; OTM has zero intrinsic value. Calls - strikes below ATM are ITM; puts - strikes above ATM are ITM. ITM premiums > OTM premiums.

name: Delta
summary: Change in premium per 1-point change in underlying; calls 0..1, puts -1..0; ATM ~0.5, ITM -> 1, OTM -> 0. First derivative of premium.
bot_use: Size option positions by net delta exposure; use delta as ITM probability for strike selection; hedge to delta-neutral.

name: Gamma
summary: Rate of change of delta per point of underlying (2nd derivative of premium); always positive for long options. Long options = long gamma; short options = short gamma.
bot_use: Risk limits should use gamma-adjusted (scenario) delta, not lot counts.

name: Theta (Time Decay)
summary: Premium lost per day from passage of time, all else equal; options are depreciating assets. Long options = negative theta; short options = positive theta (friend of sellers).

name: Premium = Intrinsic Value + Time Value
summary: Premium splits into intrinsic value (exercise value now) and time value (compensation to writer for time risk).

name: Volatility (standard deviation of returns)
summary: Volatility = risk = standard deviation of (log) returns, expressed as %; higher SD = wider expected range.

name: Standard Deviation and Variance
summary: Variance = mean of squared deviations from mean; SD = sqrt(variance); measures dispersion/consistency.

name: Normal Distribution and Price Ranges
summary: Daily returns are a random walk but approximately normally distributed; ~68% within 1 SD, 95% within 2 SD, 99.7% within 3 SD; outside 3 SD = black swan.
bot_use: Expected-move bands for strike selection, stop placement and position risk.
caveats: Real returns have fat tails - black swans happen more often than normal implies.

name: SD-Based OTM Option Writing (author's method)
summary: Compute 1-SD (or 2-SD) expected range to expiry and sell options outside it; author sells only calls, ~1 SD away, on the Friday before expiry week.

conditions.sell_puts: strikes below lower bound (author avoids puts - panic spreads faster than greed)
conditions.timing: last Friday before expiry week (~4-7 days to expiry); never > 15 days to expiry; use 2SD if writing earlier
conditions.avoid: events - monetary policy, results, policy decisions
conditions.exit: when written option turns ATM, or sentiment turns
conditions.instruments: Nifty, Bank Nifty, SBI, Infosys, Reliance, Tata Steel, Tata Motors, TCS (liquid only)

bot_use: Weekly premium-selling bot with SD strike selection, event calendar filter and ATM-touch exit.
caveats: Small steady gains
rare catastrophic losses; keep costs minimal; paper-trade several expiries first.

name: Volatility-Based Stop Loss
summary: Place stop outside expected noise - entry minus (daily vol x sqrt(holding days)) - instead of a fixed %; re-check RRR with the new stop.
bot_use: Default stop model for swing strategies.

name: Volatility Types - Historical, Forecast, Implied, Realised; India VIX
summary: Historical (from past prices), forecast (models such as GARCH(1,1)), implied (market consensus embedded in premium - most valued), realised (actual over the period). India VIX = NSE's 30-day implied vol of Nifty options ('fear index').
bot_use: Regime filter (VIX level/percentile) for buying vs selling options; IV rank for strategy choice.

name: Volatility Cone
summary: Plot min/-2SD/-1SD/mean/+1SD/+2SD/max of historical realised vol for different windows to expiry (10..90 days); overlay current IVs to spot rich (near +2SD -> short) or cheap (near -2SD -> buy) options.

conditions.short_vol: current IV >= +2SD of realised vol for same days-to-expiry

bot_use: Relative-value IV signal across strikes and underlyings.
caveats: Use only for liquid options.

name: Black-Scholes Option Pricing
summary: Inputs - spot (or futures for futures-based options), strike, risk-free rate (RBI 91-day T-bill), implied volatility, dividend (if ex-date before expiry), calendar days to expiry; outputs theoretical call/put prices and Greeks.

formula.call: S e^{-qT} N(d1) - K e^{-rT} N(d2)
formula.put: K e^{-rT} N(-d2) - S e^{-qT} N(-d1)

name: Put-Call Parity
summary: For European options of same strike/expiry - put + spot = PV(strike) + call; at expiry put + spot = strike + call.
bot_use: Detect mispricing / synthetic positions (synthetic long = long call + short put).

name: Strike Selection by Series Half and Target Time
summary: Which strike to buy depends on when in the series you trade and how fast the target is expected.

conditions.general: buy options when vol expected to rise; sell when expected to fall; don't buy far OTM just because cheap - needs a fast move

bot_use: Map signal horizon & days-to-expiry to strike offset automatically.

name: Event Volatility Play (short straddle before event, exit before announcement)
summary: IV rises into scheduled events (RBI policy, results); short ATM call + put a few days before and buy back as IV drops - ideally minutes before/at the announcement. Long straddles into events often lose because the losing leg's premium collapses faster than the winning leg gains.

conditions.entry: 2-4 days before known event, IV elevated, short ATM CE + ATM PE (liquid)
conditions.exit: time-based stop - just before announcement (or right after, as IV collapses)

bot_use: Event-calendar driven vol-selling strategy with time exits.

name: View -> Option Strategy Map
summary: Map outlook and volatility view to a strategy.
bot_use: Rule table for an options strategy engine keyed on direction signal strength + IV regime + days to expiry.

name: Bull Call Spread (debit)
summary: Moderately bullish - buy ATM (lower) call, sell OTM (higher) call, same expiry/underlying/quantity; caps profit to reduce cost.

conditions.strike_first_half: target in 5d -> far OTM pair; 15d -> slightly OTM; 25d/expiry -> ATM
conditions.strike_second_half: 1-5d -> far OTM; 10d -> slightly OTM; expiry -> ATM

name: Bull Put Spread (credit)
summary: Moderately bullish after a fall when put premiums/IV are high and time is ample - buy OTM put, sell ITM put.

name: Call Ratio Back Spread
summary: Outright bullish - sell 1 ITM call, buy 2 OTM calls (strict 2:1), usually for net credit; unlimited upside, small profit if market falls, max loss at higher strike.

conditions.strikes: slightly ITM short + slightly OTM long when time is ample; in 2nd half use deep ITM short + slightly ITM long
conditions.volatility: rising IV helps with ample time; hurts with few days left; avoid starting when IV > ~2x normal

name: Bear Call Ladder (actually bullish)
summary: Sell 1 ITM call, buy 1 ATM and 1 OTM call (1:1:1) for net credit; profits big above upper breakeven, modest if market falls, loses if market stalls; best on stocks around quarterly results.

formula.max_loss: (ATM - ITM strike) - net_credit, between ATM and OTM strikes

name: Synthetic Long (and PCP Arbitrage)
summary: Long ATM call + short ATM put replicates long futures (linear payoff); breakeven = strike + net premium. Arbitrage - synthetic long + short futures should net zero at expiry; a positive locked P&L after costs is an arbitrage.

formula.arbitrage: C(K) - P(K) - F + (F - K) ... P&L at expiry = (F - K) - (C - P) ; trade if > costs

name: Bear Put Spread (debit)
summary: Moderately bearish (~4-5% fall) - buy ITM put, sell OTM put.

name: Bear Call Spread (credit)
summary: Moderately bearish after a rally when call premiums are rich - buy OTM call, sell ITM call.

name: Put Ratio Back Spread
summary: Outright bearish - sell 1 ITM put, buy 2 OTM puts (2:1) for net credit; unlimited downside profit, limited profit if market rises; never execute for a net debit.

name: Long / Short Straddle
summary: Long - buy ATM call + ATM put (delta neutral) to profit from a large move either way; short - sell both to profit from range-bound markets / falling IV.

conditions.long_requires: low IV at entry, IV rising, large quick move before expiry, event outcome far from expectations
conditions.short_requires: high IV at entry, IV falling during hold (e.g. sell before events, exit at announcement)

caveats: Long straddles bought into events often lose due to IV crush; theta hurts longs; deltas drift as market moves - dynamic re-hedging needed to stay neutral.

name: Long / Short Strangle
summary: Like a straddle with OTM call and put (equidistant, equal lots) - cheaper but wider breakevens; short strangle sells OTM wings to collect premium in ranges.

conditions.short_strangle_setup: stock in trading range (double/triple tops-bottoms) - write strikes outside range, watch for breakouts

name: Max Pain (Option Pain)
summary: Strike at which total intrinsic payout to option buyers (loss to writers) is minimum; theory says expiry gravitates there.

formula.writer_loss_at_S: sum_over_strikes(call_OI_k * max(0, S - k) + put_OI_k * max(0, k - S))

conditions.author_variant: compute at ~15 days to expiry; add +5% buffer; expect expiry between max_pain and max_pain*1.05; write calls beyond the buffer; avoid writing puts; hold to expiry, no averaging

caveats: Controversial
no academic backing; the 5% buffer ~1.5-2 SD; backtest before use.

name: Put-Call Ratio (PCR)
summary: Total put OI / total call OI; contrarian sentiment indicator.
caveats: Calibrate extremes per instrument from 1-2 years of history; some use volume or traded value. Source's key-takeaway wording ('>1.3 bearish') refers to the crowd's positioning
interpretation is contrarian.

name: Classifying Market Income (Investor vs Trader)
summary: Heads - LTCG, STCG, speculative business income (intraday equity), non-speculative business income (all F&O - equity, currency, commodity - and frequent delivery trading). You can be both investor and trader; keep portfolios demarcated and classification consistent across years.

conditions.stcg: equity delivery held 1 day to 1 year, low frequency
conditions.non_speculative_business: F&O (any segment) or high-frequency delivery trading (e.g. several times a week)

name: Capital Gains Tax on Equity and Mutual Funds (source era)
summary: LTCG on listed equity/equity MFs via exchange (STT paid) 0%; STCG 15%. Off-market - LTCG 10% listed / 20% unlisted, STCG at slab. Debt/non-equity MFs - long-term after 3 years at 20% with indexation, else slab.
bot_use: Tax-aware exit timing (holding-period counter); after-tax backtest returns.
caveats: Current law differs (verify): LTCG on listed equity taxable above an exemption limit since 2018; STCG and LTCG rates revised in 2024.

name: Indexation (Cost Inflation Index)
summary: Inflates purchase cost by CII to tax only real gains on debt funds, property, gold etc.
caveats: Indexation benefit removed for many assets in 2023-24 changes - verify.

name: Loss Set-off and Carry-forward Rules
summary: Must file on time to carry forward. Non-speculative (F&O) loss - same year vs any income except salary; carried forward 8 years vs non-speculative business income only. Speculative (intraday) loss - only vs speculative gains, carried 4 years. STCL - vs capital gains, 8 years.

name: Tax Loss Harvesting
summary: Near financial year-end, book unrealised losses (and re-enter the position) to offset realised gains and defer tax outgo.
bot_use: Year-end (March) routine to realise losses against realised gains, respecting wash-trade/regulatory concerns.

name: Business Turnover and Tax Audit (44AB / 44AD)
summary: Audit if trading business turnover > Rs 1 Cr, or (44AD) turnover < 1 Cr but profit < 8% of turnover (unless total income below taxable limit). Trading turnover is not contract value.

formula.delivery_turnover: sell value (only if delivery trades declared as business)
formula.intraday_turnover: sum of absolute profits and losses
formula.fno_turnover: sum of absolute favourable/unfavourable differences + premium received on option sales

caveats: Thresholds changed (e.g. higher audit limits for mostly-digital receipts; ICAI guidance on F&O turnover revised in 2022) - verify.

name: Currency Pairs, Quotes and Pips
summary: Quoted as BASE/QUOTE = units of quote per 1 base; buying the pair = long base, short quote (dual view). Two-way quote bid/ask (e.g. EUR/USD 1.1269/70); a pip is the minimum move (USDINR 0.0025).

name: RBI Reference Rate and Cross Rates
summary: RBI polls randomly selected contributing banks for USDINR two-way quotes daily (11:30-12:30) and averages them; EURINR/GBPINR/JPYINR are derived by crossing through USD. Currency futures settle on the reference rate.
caveats: Reference rate is now published by FBIL
not RBI - verify.

name: Interest Rate Parity, Forward Premia and the 'Fairy' Carry Trade
summary: Borrowing in a low-rate currency to invest in a high-rate one (carry trade) is neutralised by the forward rate; the higher-yielding currency trades at a forward discount.

name: Correlation
summary: -1..+1 measure of co-movement of two series; compute on returns (stationary) not prices (trending); says direction tendency, not magnitude.

name: Seasonality Test (Holt-Winters) on USDINR
summary: Comparing Holt-Winters models with vs without seasonal component (chi-square on errors) found no weekly or monthly seasonality in USDINR - it behaves like a random walk; treat 'it always falls in December' claims as noise.
bot_use: Validate any calendar/seasonal edge statistically before trading it.

name: MCX Commodity Futures (general rules)
summary: MCX (metals, energy, some agri) and NCDEX (agri); prices include import duties/taxes; most contracts physically deliverable - intent to deliver must be given before tender period (brokers often force exit before); each contract maps to a designated spot delivery centre; trade the current/near month for liquidity; agri traded till 5 PM, no MIS for agri.
caveats: Specs as of 2016-17; MCX crude now references WTI-linked pricing and many specs changed - verify.

name: Gold - Pricing and Drivers
summary: International price set by London AM/PM fix (banks only); Indian price = international + CIF + customs duty + cess + bank costs, so MCX vs CME gold differences are not arbitrage. Gold is a safe haven - rises on uncertainty (e.g. Brexit), inversely related to the US dollar (not always), long-run ~8% CAGR in USD (1970-2016).

name: Crude Oil - Drivers and Ecosystem
summary: 2014-16 crash ($110 -> $28) driven by US shale supply, OPEC failing to cut, China slowdown, and heavy shorts; oil-producer breakevens (Russia needs ~$105) and fiscal stress. Upstream (ONGC, Cairn, RIL, Oil India) benefits from high oil; downstream OMCs (BPCL, HPCL, IOC) benefit from low oil; midstream wants stability.
bot_use: Cross-asset signals - crude moves for OMC vs upstream stock pairs; EIA release event risk.

name: Commodity Options (options on futures)
summary: Underlying is the commodity futures contract; price with Black-76 (not Black-Scholes); European; on expiry ITM options devolve into futures at the strike. CTM = 2 strikes above/below ATM (by daily settlement price) - need explicit instruction to exercise else worthless; other ITM auto-exercise unless contrary instruction; devolvement margin collected in the days before expiry.

formula.black76_call: e^{-rT} [F N(d1) - K N(d2)], d1 = (ln(F/K) + sigma^2 T/2)/(sigma sqrt T)

name: Expected Portfolio Return
summary: Weighted sum of asset expected returns; a probabilistic expectation, not a guarantee. Annualise daily mean x 252.

name: Variance, Covariance and Correlation Matrices
summary: Variance = dispersion of an asset's returns; covariance = co-movement sign of two assets; correlation = covariance / (sd_x sd_y). For k assets build the k x k variance-covariance matrix from the n x k excess-return matrix X, then the correlation matrix.

formula.cov_matrix: (1/n) * X^T X, X = returns - column means

name: Portfolio Variance (Risk)
summary: Portfolio volatility from weights, individual SDs and the correlation matrix; equivalently the SD of the portfolio's own daily returns (equity curve) - both give the same number.
caveats: Short look-back in a bull market biases expected returns upward; use >= 1 year of data.

name: Equity Curve
summary: Portfolio value normalised to Rs 100 over time (each holding compounding its daily returns at its weight); visualises performance, benchmark against Nifty; SD of its daily returns = portfolio volatility.
bot_use: Core performance artefact for any strategy/portfolio; derive drawdown, volatility, Sharpe.

name: Portfolio Optimisation and Efficient Frontier
summary: Varying weights changes risk and return. Solve (e.g. Excel Solver) for minimum-variance portfolio (min sd s.t. sum w = 1), and for each fixed risk level the max- and min-return portfolios; the upper envelope from the min-variance point is the efficient frontier - always choose portfolios on it.

formula.min_variance: min_w sqrt(w^T Sigma w) s.t. sum(w) = 1
formula.max_return_at_risk: max_w w^T mu s.t. sum(w)=1, sqrt(w^T Sigma w) = target

bot_use: Allocate across strategies/assets on the efficient frontier given a risk budget.
caveats: Add no-short (w >= 0) constraints for long-only; optimisation is sensitive to estimated returns.

name: Value at Risk (VaR) and CVaR (historical)
summary: Worst expected daily loss at a confidence level; historical method - check returns look normal (histogram), sort returns, VaR = worst value within best 95% of observations, CVaR = average of the worst 5%.
bot_use: Daily risk report and pre-trade risk limit (portfolio VaR <= budget).

name: Recovery Trauma (drawdown recovery math)
summary: Gains needed to recover a loss grow non-linearly - small accounts that take big bets suffer most. Stay in the game ('if you lose all your chips you can't bet' - Larry Hite).
bot_use: Hard max-drawdown circuit breakers; reduce size during drawdowns.

name: Position Sizing Techniques
summary: Decide how much capital/risk each trade gets. Methods - unit per fixed amount (e.g. 1 lot per 1L - simple, ignores risk, doesn't scale); percentage margin (fixed % of equity as margin per trade); percentage volatility (cap ATR-based volatility per position, e.g. 2% of equity); percentage risk (cap loss-at-stop at 1-3% of equity). Combine one equity model with one or two sizing methods.

formula.classic_5pct_rule: max exposure per trade = 5% of capital

bot_use: Mandatory sizing layer between signal and order - default to % risk with ATR/volatility stops, reduced-total-equity accounting.

name: Kelly Criterion (and capped Kelly)
summary: Optimal bet fraction from win rate and win/loss ratio; author scales a capped risk budget by Kelly% rather than betting full Kelly.
bot_use: Scale per-trade risk by rolling backtest/live Kelly, capped.
caveats: Full Kelly is too aggressive - a 70% Kelly still leaves a large chance of a huge loss; estimates of W and R are noisy.

name: Trading Journal
summary: Record why each trade was entered and exited to learn from your own behaviour and overcome attribution bias.
bot_use: Log every signal, filter decision, order, fill and exit reason for post-trade analysis.

name: Backtesting
summary: Running a system's rules over historical data to measure frequency, win rate and P&L profile before risking capital; use clean, corporate-action-adjusted, date-aligned data; backtest per instrument and per direction (e.g. SBIN calendar spreads - shorts worked, longs mixed).
bot_use: Every node with 'conditions' should be backtested with realistic costs/slippage before deployment.

name: Pair Trading Method 1 - Ratio z-score / Density Curve (Mark Whistler)
summary: Track ratio = price_A / price_B; compute mean, SD (and SD table up to +/-3), and the cumulative normal 'density curve' value NORM.DIST(ratio, mean, sd, TRUE) daily; trade extremes, exit toward mean.

conditions.long_pair: density in ~[0.003, 0.025] (ratio at -2..-3 SD) -> buy A (numerator), sell B
conditions.short_pair: density in ~[0.975, 0.997] (+2..+3 SD) -> sell A, buy B
conditions.exit: ratio back inside 2 SD / toward mean (e.g. density ~0.16-0.84)

caveats: Correlation of Axis-ICICI only ~0.5 in example; author considers this method a foundation - prefers regression method; consider rupee neutrality.

name: Linear Regression (for pairs)
summary: Fit y = M*x + c (+ residual) between two price series; outputs slope (beta/hedge ratio), intercept, residuals, standard error (SD of residuals) and standard error of intercept.

name: Error Ratio (choose X vs Y)
summary: Regress both ways; pick the orientation with the lower error ratio (keeps intercept - the unhedged part - small).

name: Stationarity, Cointegration and the ADF Test
summary: Two prices are cointegrated if the regression residuals are stationary (constant mean, constant SD, no autocorrelation); test with Augmented Dickey-Fuller - p-value is probability of NON-stationarity; require p <= 0.05. Regression relations on non-stationary residuals are spurious.

conditions.manual_checks: means of 3 sub-samples similar; SDs similar; lag-1/lag-2 autocorrelation ~0

bot_use: Weekly/biweekly re-screen of sector pairs (200-day lookback) with statsmodels.adfuller.

name: Pair Trading Method 2 - Regression Residual z-score (Stat Arb)
summary: For same-sector pairs over 200 days - regress both ways, keep lower error ratio orientation, require ADF p <= 0.05, then trade the residual's z-score with beta-neutral quantities.

formula.qty_x: qty_y * beta (round to lot sizes; top up in cash market if needed)

conditions.skip: negative beta (often untradeable); large intercept relative to price_y (e.g. 1626/2024 = 80% unexplained)

bot_use: Complete stat-arb pipeline - nightly screen, z-score monitor intraday, beta-neutral sizing, z-based exits.

name: Statistical Futures Calendar Spread
summary: Treat the next-month minus current-month futures price difference as a mean-reverting series (prices already embed carry, dividends etc.); trade +/-1 SD deviations back to the mean.

conditions.sell_spread: spread > mean + 1sd -> sell next month, buy current month
conditions.buy_spread: spread < mean - 1sd -> buy next month, sell current month

name: Cross-Sectional Momentum Portfolio
summary: From a tracking universe (e.g. BSE 500, or custom filters like mcap >= 1000 Cr; 150-200 stocks for a 12-15 stock portfolio), rank by trailing 12-month return, buy top 10-15 equally weighted on the first trading day of the month, rebalance monthly (sell drop-outs, buy new entrants).

conditions.entry: top N by 12m return, equal weight
conditions.rebalance: monthly after close on last trading day
conditions.variations: 1m/2w/1w lookbacks; skewed weights; fundamental momentum (quarterly sales growth, EPS growth, margins) rebalanced quarterly

bot_use: Monthly rebalancing bot with index-trend regime filter (e.g. Nifty above 200-DMA).
caveats: Works in up-trending markets; poor in choppy markets; bleeds more than the market in downtrends (author profited 2009-10
hit in 2011) - add a market regime filter; backtest first.

name: Simple vs Compound Interest
summary: Simple interest only on principal; compound interest on principal plus accumulated interest.

name: Retirement Corpus Planning
summary: Inflate today's annual expense for each retirement year (FV at inflation ~5%) and sum to get the corpus; build it via monthly SIPs into equity funds with annual step-ups, each instalment compounding for its remaining months.

name: SEBI Equity Fund Categories
summary: Market-cap classes - large cap = top 100 by full market cap, mid cap = 101-250, small cap = 251+. Large-cap funds >= 80% large caps; large & mid >= 35% each; also multi-cap, focused (max 30 stocks), dividend yield, ELSS (tax-saving, 3-yr lock-in), sectoral/thematic.
bot_use: Universe definitions for large/mid/small-cap strategies (rank by full market cap).

name: Market Capitalisation
summary: Share price x shares outstanding; market cap of the whole market tends to grow with GDP.

name: Return Measurement (Absolute, CAGR, XIRR, Rolling)
summary: Lump-sum or SIP < 1 yr - absolute return; lump sum > 1 yr - CAGR; SIP > 1 yr - XIRR (cash-flow-dated IRR). Point-to-point returns depend on the two dates; rolling n-year returns (CAGR for every start date) show the distribution - use average, min, max.

formula.rolling_n: for each date t: (nav_t / nav_{t - n years}) ** (1/n) - 1

bot_use: Evaluate strategies with rolling-window returns, not single point-to-point backtests.

name: Benchmarking and Total Return Index (TRI)
summary: Compare against TRI (price + dividends reinvested), not price index; index returns depend on constituent weights; set realistic personal benchmarks.
bot_use: Benchmark strategies against Nifty 50 TRI.

name: Risk-Adjusted Performance Metrics (Beta, Alpha, SD, Sharpe, Sortino, Capture Ratios)
summary: Beta = relative risk vs benchmark (not inherent risk); alpha = risk-adjusted excess return; SD = inherent volatility; Sharpe = excess return per unit total volatility; Sortino = per unit downside deviation; capture ratios = share of benchmark up/down moves captured - prefer consistent low downside capture.
bot_use: Standard strategy scorecard - Sharpe, Sortino, beta/alpha vs Nifty, capture ratios, max drawdown.
caveats: Sharpe is meaningless for debt funds (ignores credit/rate risk).

name: Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs)
summary: Exchange-traded index/commodity/debt wrappers with creation/redemption by market makers/APs; liquidity layers - screen depth, market makers, primary creation, underlying stocks (illiquid underlyings -> premiums/discounts).

conditions.always: use limit orders; compare price with iNAV/underlying index; avoid first 30-60 min after open; check average volumes and tracking vs TRI; prefer AMCs serious about ETFs; create units with AMC for large tickets

bot_use: Limit-order execution guard - never market-order an ETF; reject if price deviates from iNAV beyond threshold.

name: GDP, Real vs Nominal Growth, and Market Cap
summary: GDP = total economic output; real growth = nominal - inflation; India ~$2.6-2.9T (5th/6th, 2020); as GDP grows, aggregate market cap tends to grow - basis for long-term equity investing.

name: Government Finances and Fiscal Deficit
summary: Revenue = tax (direct - personal/corporate income tax; indirect - GST) + non-tax (PSU dividends, disinvestment); expenditure = revenue (subsidies, salaries, interest) + capital (infrastructure). Fiscal deficit = expenditure - revenue; India FY19 ~3.3% of GDP (govt aims < 4%); higher capex share and tax-to-GDP are positive signals.

name: Integrated Financial Model
summary: A linked workbook that takes financial statements as input and outputs a valuation (fair share price); fully integrated, so changing any assumption flows through P&L, balance sheet, cash flow and DCF. Modelling is part art (assumptions) and part craft (structure).
bot_use: Generates a fair value per share and lets you run sensitivity scenarios; feeds margin-of-safety screens and long-horizon value bots. Recompute after every annual/quarterly report.

name: Assumption Sheet - Ratio/Growth Drivers with Rolling Averages
summary: Express each line item historically as a ratio to a driver (BS items vs gross block; P&L items vs sales) or as a YoY growth rate; project with the rolling average of the last 4 years (Y6 = avg(Y2..Y5), Y7 = avg(Y3..Y6)) or an informed guess. Prefer drivers with a narrow, stable historical range.

formula.deferred_tax: deferred_tax = avg(deferred_tax / depreciation) * depreciation (more stable than growth)

name: Inventory and Receivable Days
summary: Convert inventory (and receivables) from rupees to days, average the days, then convert back for projections; the days figures also reveal operating efficiency (fewer days = faster conversion to sales).

name: Revenue Sub-model
summary: Build revenue bottom-up from common-sense questions answered in the annual report - what they make, where they sell (domestic vs export), units x realisation per unit, capacity and utilisation. It also yields capacity utilisation, capex cycles and market share.

name: Base Rule (Roll-forward)
summary: Every schedule rolls forward - this year's closing balance is next year's opening balance; closing = opening + additions - deletions.

name: Asset Schedule (Gross Block, CAPEX, Depreciation, Net Block)
summary: Back out historical capex from changes in gross block; project capex from management guidance (best), historical averages, or a variable method; project depreciation with the proportion method (depreciation/gross block); roll accumulated depreciation forward; the net block flows back to the balance sheet and the depreciation to the P&L.

name: Debt Schedule
summary: Split debt into secured and unsecured using the notes, average the opening and closing balances to get the interest base, and project debt from management's capex/financing view; with no guidance, hold debt flat.

name: Equity / Reserves Schedule
summary: Share capital (authorised >= issued >= subscribed/paid-up; shares = share capital / face value); reserves - securities premium (rises with fresh equity), general reserve, retained earnings (PAT flows in, dividends and DDT flow out). This is the main P&L-to-BS link.

name: Indirect Cash Flow and Balance Check
summary: Derive cash flow from P&L and balance-sheet changes - CFO (PAT + depreciation from the asset schedule +/- working-capital changes), CFI (capex, investments), CFF (debt, equity, dividends). Net cash flow plus opening cash gives closing cash, which plugs into the balance sheet; if the model is integrated correctly the balance sheet balances.

name: Valuation Approaches (Relative, Option-based, Absolute)
summary: Relative - value like identical peers via multiples (fails if the sector is mispriced or the companies differ). Option-based - the firm's value depends on an event (e.g. R&D success), valued like an option (niche, tech). Absolute - intrinsic value from discounted cash flow (enterprise or equity). Decision - market price > fair price means overvalued, < means undervalued.

name: Enterprise Value and Equity Value
summary: Rearranging the balance sheet - fixed assets = net debt + equity. Valuing the whole firm gives EV (discount FCFF at WACC); EV - debt + cash = equity value; divide by shares outstanding for fair value per share.

name: Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF) and to Equity (FCFE)
summary: The firm is financed by debt and equity holders; FCFF is the cash available to both, and FCFE is what remains for equity after debt service. Discount FCFF at WACC and FCFE at the cost of equity.

formula.fcff_from_pat: PAT + D&A + interest*(1-tax) + deferred_tax - delta_working_capital - capex

name: Interest Tax Shield / Effective Cost of Debt
summary: Interest is tax-deductible, so its after-tax cost is lower; add back interest*(1-t) in FCFF and use the after-tax cost of debt in WACC.

name: CAPM - Cost of Equity
summary: The return equity holders expect is the risk-free rate plus beta times the market risk premium. Proxy Rf with the 10-year G-sec yield (CCIL/RBI); the long-term market return Rm is ~8-12%.

name: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC)
summary: A blended discount rate for the whole firm; the cost of equity is always above WACC.

name: Terminal Value (Gordon Growth)
summary: Beyond the 5 explicit years, assume cash flows grow forever at roughly long-term inflation; DCF is extremely sensitive to this number, and it requires stable positive cash flows (DCF fails with negative ones).

name: DCF Implementation in the Model
summary: Inputs are Rf (10Y G-sec, ~7%), Rm (10-12%), beta, kd (~10%), tax (25%), target D/E (50%) and terminal g (~inflation). Steps - project FCFF Y6-Y10, compute TV at Y10, discount everything at WACC, sum to EV, subtract debt and add cash to get equity value, divide by shares for the fair price, then compare with the market price and run sensitivities on key assumptions.
bot_use: fair_value(inputs) -> upside = fair/price - 1; screen for upside > margin_of_safety; run grid sensitivity on g and WACC.

name: Insurance (Risk Transfer) - basics
summary: Insurance transfers the financial risk of rare, high-cost events to an insurer in exchange for a premium; health and term life insurance come before an emergency fund and before investing. Insurers price risk through pooling and are exposed to adverse selection and moral hazard, which explains most policy restrictions.
bot_use: Capital-protection precondition - a trading account should never be the emergency or medical fund.

name: Full Medical Disclosure (Non-disclosure risk)
summary: Declare every pre-existing condition and habit directly to the insurer on the proposal form - never rely on an agent's verbal assurance. Non-disclosure lets the insurer repudiate the claim or cancel the policy; a loading charge and a waiting period are far better than a rejected claim.

conditions.rule: disclose all medical history, medication, smoking/alcohol on the form itself

name: Co-payment Clause
summary: You pay a fixed % of every claim (e.g. 20%) in exchange for a lower premium - gives you 'skin in the game'. Usually a bad trade.

conditions.avoid_unless: mandatory, or buying for elderly with pre-existing diseases where it cuts premium sharply

name: Room Rent Cap / Proportionate Deduction
summary: A cap on room rent (e.g. 1% of sum insured per day). Choosing a costlier room makes the insurer pay proportionately on all room-linked charges (surgeon, consultant, diagnostics), not only the rent difference.

conditions.prefer: no room-rent cap; at least single private room allowed

name: Permanent Exclusions, Sub-limits, Non-medical Items, Blacklisted Hospitals
summary: Insurer defences against abuse - permanent exclusions (substance/alcohol-induced illness, cosmetic treatment, external congenital conditions); disease-wise sub-limits (e.g. cardiac Rs 2.5L, knee Rs 2.75L, cataract Rs 50k regardless of cover) - avoid policies with them; non-medical consumables excluded; only 'just and reasonable' treatment per medical council norms paid; blacklisted hospitals can be refused.

conditions.check_before_buying: no disease-wise sub-limits; read permanent exclusion list; check hospital blacklist; get a second opinion for expensive procedures

name: Group and Employer Health Insurance
summary: Customised contracts for a group via a master policyholder (bank, employer). Cheaper and often with no waiting periods (invaluable for those with serious PEDs), but pricing is repriced yearly at the insurer's discretion, features are set by the master policyholder, and cover ends if you leave the job or the group dissolves (re-underwriting then). Keep a personal policy alongside an employer cover.

conditions.rule: employer cover + personal base policy (or a super top-up aligned to the employer cover)

name: Super Top-up Health Plan
summary: Very cheap large cover (e.g. Rs 50 lakh for ~Rs 1,000s/yr) that pays once the aggregate bills within a policy year cross the deductible. Choose the deductible equal to the existing base or employer cover, and align policy-year dates with that cover, otherwise the deductible must be met again in a new term.

formula.payout: max(0, sum(claims_in_policy_year) - deductible), capped at cover

conditions.dates: super top-up renewal aligned with base/employer policy year

name: Claim Settlement Ratio (CSR) and Incurred Claims Ratio (ICR)
summary: CSR = % of claims settled; it can be gamed (clearing last year's backlog, settling many small claims while rejecting large ones, combining motor/health for general insurers). Read it alongside ICR and scale (large customer base). Get the numbers from the IRDAI annual report.

conditions.icr_high: >100% -> insurer losing money (regulator may force merger)
conditions.icr_low: ~50% -> may be stingy on large claims
